$comment: THE ORTHOGRAPHY. No orthographic rule is written in application code (invariant 1) — the engine in lib/engine/ is an interpreter over this file, and it exists in this form so that a Bugis-literate reviewer who does not program can audit it. `pnpm rules:report` prints it as a readable table. Every rule carries a citation (invariant 2); `status` says what kind of citation it is, and `provisional` rules are the ones a reviewer should attack first. Things this repo will not rule on are listed under openQuestions rather than guessed at.
$ambiguityClassesComment: A CLOSED SET (invariant 3). Adding a class is a deliberate schema change, not a convenience. All four follow from the absence of a virama in the encoding.

final.description: A syllable-final consonant is not written.

gemination.description: A single consonant and a doubled consonant are written alike.

prenasal.description: Prenasalisation is not written where no prenasal letter covers the cluster.

glottal.description: The glottal stop is not written.

rules.citation: Unicode: every letter in the Buginese block has general category Lo and no case mappings — the script is unicameral, so Latin case carries no information the script can record.
rules.description: Fold Latin input to lower case.

rules.citation: Unicode Standard: U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK and U+02BC MODIFIER LETTER APOSTROPHE are the two characters commonly typed or substituted where U+0027 APOSTROPHE is meant. Typographic normalisation of the input, not an orthographic claim.
rules.description: Normalise apostrophe-like characters to U+0027, which is how the glottal stop is written in Bugis Latin — the apostrophe in Lontara'.

rules.citation: The Unicode character name for U+1A13 is BUGINESE LETTER VA, which is why `v` is the primary onset in inventory.json. `w` is accepted as an input spelling for the same letter.
rules.note: PROVISIONAL AND UNVERIFIED. Whether Bugis Latin practice writes this onset `w` or `v` — or whether both occur — is not established in this repository, and the Unicode character name is evidence about the encoding rather than about Bugis Latin orthography. This rule only widens what is accepted as input; it never changes what is written out. A reviewer should rule on it. See openQuestions.va-latin.
rules.description: Accept `w` as input for the onset written by U+1A13 BUGINESE LETTER VA.

rules.citation: Derived from inventory.json: the block has no virama (block.hasVirama = false), so the script writes only (C)V units — a consonant letter carrying the inherent vowel /a/, optionally with a vowel sign replacing it. A Latin form is therefore parsed as the longest onset present in inventory.consonants followed by a vowel; a consonant that cannot begin such a unit is syllable-final. The derivation is stated here in full so it can be disputed as a whole rather than accepted piecemeal.
rules.description: Parse Latin into (C)V units, longest onset first. Leftover consonants are syllable-final.

rules.citation: Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf, block Buginese. Each consonant letter U+1A00..U+1A16 carries the inherent vowel /a/; a vowel sign U+1A17..U+1A1B replaces it. The Latin value of each letter and sign is its Unicode character name.
rules.description: Write a (C)V unit as its consonant letter, plus a vowel sign unless the vowel is the inherent /a/. A vowel with no onset takes U+1A15 BUGINESE LETTER A as its carrier.

rules.citation: Unicode character names U+1A03 BUGINESE LETTER NGKA, U+1A07 MPA, U+1A0B NRA, U+1A0F NYCA. These four letters write a nasal+stop onset as a single letter, so those four clusters are written rather than lost.
rules.description: Where a nasal+stop cluster is covered by one of the four prenasal letters, write that letter. Nothing is lost in this case.

rules.citation: Derived from inventory.json block.hasVirama = false and PRD §2 (`mata` / `matta` / `manta` are written identically). A syllable-final consonant identical to the onset of the syllable that follows it is a geminate; with no virama there is no way to write it, so it collapses into the single following letter.
rules.trigger: final consonant identical to the following onset
rules.description: A geminate is written as a single letter. The doubling is not recoverable from the writing.

rules.citation: Derived from inventory.json and PRD §2. Where a nasal is syllable-final before a stop and the cluster is NOT one of the four written by U+1A03/U+1A07/U+1A0B/U+1A0F, no letter in the block writes it, so the nasal is not written.
rules.note: The choice this rule records is a real open question, not a settled one. Four prenasal clusters ARE written, which sits in tension with PRD §2's flat statement that prenasalisation is not written. Whether Bugis practice extends a prenasal letter to other nasal+stop clusters, writes the nasal some other way, or omits it, is unresolved here — so the writer emits an Ambiguity of class `prenasal` with this rule as its stated reason rather than passing over it in silence. See openQuestions.prenasal-coverage.
rules.trigger: final nasal before a stop, cluster not covered by a prenasal letter
rules.description: An unwritten prenasalising nasal is dropped, and the loss is declared at that span.

rules.citation: Derived from inventory.json block.hasVirama = false and PRD §2. There is no mechanism in the encoding for a bare consonant, so any consonant that closes a syllable is not written.
rules.trigger: syllable-final consonant not matched by a higher-priority loss rule
rules.description: A syllable-final consonant is dropped, and the loss is declared at that span.

rules.citation: Derived from inventory.json: no character in the block writes a glottal stop, and there is no virama. PRD §2 lists the glottal stop among what the orthography does not write; PRD §6.7 identifies the apostrophe in Lontara' as how Bugis Latin writes it.
rules.trigger: U+0027 APOSTROPHE in normalised Latin input
rules.description: The glottal stop is dropped, and the loss is declared at that span.

openQuestions.question: Does Bugis Latin write the onset of U+1A13 BUGINESE LETTER VA as `w`, as `v`, or both depending on the source?
openQuestions.why: inventory.json takes `v` from the Unicode character name, which is evidence about the encoding and not about Bugis Latin orthography. `w` is accepted on input as provisional. Getting this wrong misspells every word containing the letter.
openQuestions.askWhom: Badan Bahasa South Sulawesi; the dictionaries in PRD Appendix A

openQuestions.question: Which Latin letter or diacritic corresponds to U+1A1B BUGINESE VOWEL SIGN AE?
openQuestions.why: The name gives `ae`, which is almost certainly not how it is written in Bugis Latin — /e/ versus /ə/ is exactly the kind of distinction PRD §6.7 says the Latin side must specify. Until it is settled, inventory.json carries `ae` from the character name with a note, and nothing prettier is invented.
openQuestions.askWhom: Badan Bahasa South Sulawesi; a Bugis reviewer

openQuestions.question: Four prenasal clusters are written with dedicated letters (ngk, mp, nr, nyc). What happens to every other nasal+stop cluster?
openQuestions.why: PRD §2 states flatly that prenasalisation is not written, but the block plainly writes four of them. Either the statement is a simplification or the four letters are used differently than their names suggest. The reader's enumeration of the `prenasal` class depends on the answer.
openQuestions.askWhom: A Bugis reviewer who reads manuscript Lontara; Everson's encoding proposals (PRD Appendix A)

openQuestions.question: Which consonants can close a syllable in Bugis, and with what relative frequency?
openQuestions.why: It would let the reader enumerate `final` readings structurally rather than only where the lexicon attests them. Deliberately NOT guessed at: a structural enumerator seeded with an invented set of possible finals would produce a confident-looking tree of readings that are not Bugis. Until the set is cited, enumeration stays lexicon-driven and says so.
openQuestions.askWhom: The dictionaries in PRD Appendix A; a Bugis reviewer

openQuestions.question: What does PALLAWA (U+1A1E) separate, and how should it and END OF SECTION (U+1A1F) be represented in Latin?
openQuestions.why: The writer cannot emit either mark and the reader cannot read one back until this is answered. inventory.json carries `latin: null` for both rather than assuming pallawa is a space.
openQuestions.askWhom: The dictionaries and textbook sources in PRD Appendix A; a Bugis reviewer

openQuestions.question: Which side do VOWEL SIGN E (U+1A19) and VOWEL SIGN O (U+1A1A) render on?
openQuestions.why: Both are spacing marks (Mc) with no UCD combining class, so the encoding does not answer it. This is a rendering question, and the conformance page answers it by eye rather than inventory.json asserting it.
openQuestions.askWhom: Nobody — check /aksara/konformansi on a real device and record the answer.
